findings.description: Strongest, unanimous (B1/B2/B3): the terse EARS phrase 'during the marks read-back pass' hides that 'the pass' is actually a bounded, multi-poll settle loop — read_marks (lib.rs:817-845) calls client.read_price_pass() repeatedly (up to SettleConfig::max_polls, default 8) until every symbol is numeric-or-terminally-errored. The code+tests pin an atomicity rule the spec text never states: a transport Err on ANY poll — the first or a later one, even after earlier polls in the SAME pass already latched good per-symbol readings into the in-progress `latest` map — voids the entire pass; `latest` is discarded via the early `?` return, nothing is merged or partially returned. B1 ('even if earlier polls... already returned good per-symbol readings'), B2 ('a transport failure on ANY iteration... no partial per-symbol readings latched earlier... merged, degraded, or returned'), and B3 ('whether on the first poll or a later one') all independently surfaced this.

Medium-agreement (B1, B3; not B2): the code+tests draw a boundary the spec text is silent on — a missing/uncreated Positions tab (fresh-workbook cold start) is explicitly classified as NOT a transport failure. read_price_pass returns Ok(empty PricePass), never Err, for this case, verified directly by runtime/tests/cold_start.rs::the_price_pass_on_a_fresh_workbook_is_empty_not_an_error. SHEET-MARK-006 says only 'if a transport failure occurs' and never defines what does or doesn't count as one; the real system pins a specific, non-obvious classification (missing-tab vs. genuinely-unreachable) that gates whether the propagate-and-emit-nothing branch fires at all.

Unanimous in substance: the code has no dedicated transport-failure error type. Real transport failure on the settle pass is represented by REUSING ViewError::PublishFailed (testkit.rs::read_price_pass: 'if *self.read_fails.borrow() { return Err(ViewError::PublishFailed); }') — the same variant used for a failed tab publish — and is structurally distinct from a per-symbol PriceReading::Transient/Permanent (both Ok values inside a successful PricePass, governed by the separate max_polls retry/degrade rules, not this requirement). The EARS text's undifferentiated 'a transport failure occurs' establishes neither the variant-reuse nor the transport-vs-per-symbol split; B2 explicitly flags 'no specific ViewError variant is pinned for this path (the trait/tests assert only .is_err())' as evidence the spec is silent on error shape while the code has made a concrete, reused choice.

Weak, single-run (B2 only): Publisher::republish_then_settle's return type Result<(RepublishOutcome, MarksProduced), ViewError> (lib.rs:1012-1025) means that when read_marks fails after a successful republish(), the whole call returns Err and the caller permanently loses the already-computed RepublishOutcome — there is no way to observe 'publish succeeded, settle failed' from this call. SHEET-MARK-006 is scoped to the read-back pass itself and says nothing about this composition; only B2 raised it, so confidence is lower, though it is directly verifiable in the given lib.rs.

notes: Direction A surfaced no material findings. All three A-outputs invent the same handful of structural details — a dedicated TransportError type, fail-fast per-row/per-symbol iteration (vs. the real code's single bulk-per-poll settle loop), and a runtime-owned MarksCache with an apply_pass/current() shape — but every one of these is self-flagged by its own author as an assumption with 'no basis in the spec text' / 'not stated by the EARS', and none of them identifies spec-stated behavior the real code fails to honor. The real sheets_view::read_marks (lib.rs:817-887), backed by tests/marks.rs::transport_failure_propagates_error_does_not_emit_empty_marks, fully implements 'propagate the error' and 'emit no marks for that pass (no partial or degraded marks)'; and runtime's MarksCache/run_cycle (referenced in lib.rs's own doc comment, lines 806-816) implements 'runtime owns carry-forward, retaining the last cached marks' by simply never replacing the cache until read_marks succeeds — almost exactly the shape A1 and A3 independently guessed. So A-side is highly stable but non-material (its inventions match reality closely enough, and where they diverge — bulk-vs-per-symbol transport shape — the divergence is explicitly acknowledged as arbitrary, not spec-forced). B-side is where the real signal is: the code+tests pin several concrete rules (multi-poll pass atomicity, cold-start-is-not-transport-failure, error-variant reuse) that the six-clause EARS sentence never states, though the three B-runs agree strongly on the core claim (propagate/no-partial/runtime-owns-carry-forward) and only partially agree on which secondary details to add (cold-start boundary in 2/3 runs, the republish_then_settle consequence in 1/3) — hence 'medium' rather than 'high' B-agreement despite a clean B-ONLY-DRIFT classification."
